body:
_Migrated from issue #1265, filed 2026-07-31._

Follow-up from #1262, which made `integration-tests` gate on what a PR touches rather than on its tier label.

Both consumers of the new signal read `needs.changed_paths.outputs.build`. If `changed_paths` **fails** rather than skips, that output is the empty string:

- `integration-tests` evaluates `needs.changed_paths.outputs.build == 'true'` to false, so a Dockerfile-only PR skips the job.
- `test-summary` computes `IS_BUILD_PR=false`, sees a `skipped` integration result, and reports success.

That is the same shape as the bug #1262 fixes — a gate whose absence reads as a pass — one level up, triggered by infrastructure instead of a missing label. `changed_paths` is a checkout plus a `git diff` with a 5-minute timeout, so this needs a genuine runner or checkout failure. Unlikely, not impossible, and the failure is silent when it happens.

**Fix: fail closed.** Treat any non-success `changed_paths` as `build=true` rather than as `build=''`, so an infrastructure failure over-runs the expensive job instead of skipping the gate. `always()` already keeps the job reachable in that state; only the predicate needs to distinguish "not a build PR" from "we could not tell".

The `e2e-tests` job reads `needs.changed_paths.outputs.frontend` with the same shape and has the same gap, so whatever lands here should cover both.

A regression test belongs in `tests/unit/test_workflow_safety_invariants.py` next to the 19 behavioural cases #1262 added.
title: CI: a failed (not skipped) changed_paths silently disables the build gate
